title: A little-endian file header
description:
Write and read a binary header byte by byte, so it works on any machine.

```
wrote header: 58 4E 01 00 20 03 00 00 58 02 00 00
read back: magic "XN", version 1, width 800, height 600
bad magic: refused
```
hints: `p[0] = v & 0xFF; p[1] = (v >> 8) & 0xFF; ...` writes the lowest byte first (lesson 5.02).
Reading: `(uint32_t)p[0] | (uint32_t)p[1] << 8 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24`. The casts stop the bytes being promoted to a signed `int`.
requirements: Fields: 2 magic bytes `XN`, a `uint16_t` version, two `uint32_t` sizes, all little-endian.
`void put_u32(uint8_t *p, uint32_t v)` and `uint32_t get_u32(const uint8_t *p)` with shifts, never `memcpy` of the struct.
Write with `fwrite` in `"wb"` mode, read with `fread`, and refuse a file whose magic is wrong.
stretch: Add a checksum byte at the end and check it when reading.
